title: Fix XMIDI tempo (4x too fast) + reconcile broken music director build
description: xmidi2smf.py hardcodes PPQN=120 calibrated to one track -> most GM tracks play ~4x too fast (agricultural base happens fine). Separately, music.h was rewritten to the np-ida dynamic director but main.cpp/music.cpp are half-migrated (main.cpp:2014 still 3-arg update) -> build broken. Fix tempo (validate every track vs its AdLib reference duration) AND reconcile the director so it compiles + plays the dynamic flight/combat/base music from docs/music_labels.json.

comments.author: Mike Pfaffenberger
comments.text:
DONE end-to-end. Both fixes shipped.

BUILD RECONCILE (path taken: COMPLETED the director, no revert):
- Rewrote src/music.cpp to implement music.h EXACTLY: full Track enum (FlightMain=combat_04, CombatFar=combat_05, CombatNear=combat_06, CombatResolve=combat_07, StingJump=combat_08, StingLanding=combat_09, StingDeath=combat_10, BaseAgricultural=basetune_00, BaseMining=basetune_04, Menu=opening_00); load_all loads those stems from assets/music/original/; 4-arg update(GameMode,pos,base_id,dt) with the flight combat-tier state machine via threat::nearest_hostile_distance (Main/Far/Near, 5km line +/-500m hysteresis, 6s combat-hold, Resolve outro timed off the WAV length then feeds FlightMain), per-base landed tune by base.json market.archetype, mode-edge stings (jump on Loading, death on Dying); 2-voice crossfade loops via play_loop (np-3va-uncullable), stings one-shot on the music bus via play; separate master bus + mute + introspection. Fixed BOTH main.cpp call sites (flight :2016 passes last_docked_base+dt, stub :1725 passes last_docked_base+sapp dur) to the 4-arg form. cmake --build build -j GREEN.

TEMPO ROOT-CAUSE (the 4x bug): XMIDI/Miles AIL runs on a FIXED 120-ticks/SECOND clock and IGNORES the embedded FF51 tempo meta. Old xmidi2smf.py emitted PPQN=120 AND passed FF51 through, so FluidSynth obeyed tempo: a 60 BPM cue = 120 ticks/s (right by luck -> base/agri tunes fine), a 140 BPM combat cue = 280 ticks/s = 2.33x fast, 142 BPM stingers faster; error = BPM/60, so most galloped while a couple were fine (single-track calibration on 60-BPM basetune_04 masked it). FIX: emit 120 ticks/s for EVERY track -> PPQN=60 + single injected 120 BPM tempo (500000 us/qtr; 1e6/500000*60=120 t/s) at tick 0, DROP source FF51. (ScummVM/Exult canonical.) Constants XMIDI_PPQN/XMIDI_FIXED_TEMPO_US in tools/xmidi2smf.py.

VALIDATION (tools/validate_music_tempo.py vs libADLMIDI AdLib refs, ALL 27 sub-songs PASS):
combat_04 .49x->1.04x, _05 .46->1.02, _06 .46->1.02, _07 .46->1.03; basetune_00 .84->1.03, _07 1.04, _10 .56->1.01; opening_00 .66->1.01; every track now == AdLib ref OR its own span/120 within synth tail. credits_00 (unused) is tempo-exact; its GM .GEN arrangement is genuinely longer than the .ADL twin (content diff, not tempo).

FILES: src/music.cpp (rewrite), src/main.cpp (2 call sites), tools/xmidi2smf.py (tempo), tools/render_music.py (mirror DIRECTOR_STEMS into asset_dir), tools/validate_music_tempo.py (new validator), docs/music_extraction.md (root-cause+fix+corrected durations).

GIT-IGNORE: all rendered WAVs (gog_extracted/music_wav + assets/music/original) ignored; tools+docs committable. Verified via git check-ignore.

RUN: ./build/new_privateer --system troy running (log /tmp/np_troy_musicfix.log): 10/10 tracks loaded at correct durations, director switched flight_main -> combat_far as a hostile entered scope, hysteresis steady (no strobe), no errors. np-3va loop-protection + sfx untouched, no new runtime deps.

title: Voice pool saturates during large Troy furball (steal-spin timeouts)
description: Under a big NPC-gunfire furball the 24-voice pool saturates and alloc_slot's steal path logs 'steal spin timed out — refusing voice' en masse. Pre-existing: the 5ms steal deadline is shorter than the ~46ms (2048-frame) buffer period, so a stolen one-shot can't retire in time whenever the pool is full. Original SFX one-shots are slightly longer than the procedural placeholders, nudging saturation up. Options: raise voice count, shrink buffer, lengthen/relax the steal deadline to ~1 buffer period, or cull more aggressively. Cosmetic today (game runs fine, designed safety valve), but worth tuning. Discovered via np-b8a.
notes:
FIXED (code-puppy-8633fe).

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis CONFIRMED + sharpened): audio::alloc_slot()'s voice-steal path busy-WAITED on the game thread. The wait cap (5ms) was SHORTER than the audio buffer period (2048 frames @ 44.1kHz = ~46ms, confirmed at boot: '[audio] device 44100Hz 2ch, 24 voices, buffer 2048 frames'), so during saturation the spin could NEVER succeed — it always burned the full 5ms then refused. All sfx fire from the game thread (firing::tick gun_fired; main.cpp damage pass impact/ship_exploded). With the full pool saturated in a furball, EACH new sound that triggered a steal stalled the game thread ~5ms; dozens/frame = tens-to-hundreds of ms of main-thread stall/frame = the lag. Original SFX (longer than placeholders: cruise_windup 3.3s, explosions, engine drone) keep voices alive far longer -> pool saturates constantly -> the regression. The existing 8/sec impact limiter WAS firing but only covered impacts; NPC gunfire had NO gate and flooded play_world unthrottled.

FIX:
1. NON-BLOCKING alloc (primary). Removed the spin entirely. New instant-steal handoff: main writes the new sound into the victim slot's pending_{sample_idx,loop} + main-owned bookkeeping, then raises an atomic 'reload' (release) LAST; the mixer consumes reload (acquire) at the top of its next pass, swaps pending->active, rewinds the cursor, and the new sound starts that same buffer. Audio thread is the SOLE writer of sample_idx/loop/cursor while a slot is live -> race free, zero wait.
2. VICTIM-PRIORITY CULL + per-frame BUDGET. Full 24-voice pool kept (not shrunk). On a full pool alloc steals the WEAKEST live non-loop voice (lowest current L/R gain, oldest on tie); loops (engine hum) NEVER eligible. Priority gate: steal only if newcomer gain >= weakest*0.9, else DROP (a distant tiny impact won't evict a louder closer sound). Per-frame budget k_max_world_starts_per_frame=8 caps NEW world one-shot starts; surplus drops. Reset in set_listener (once/frame).
3. DEDUP/COALESCE. Added NPC-gunfire coalescing in sfx.cpp (~12/sec, mirrors impact gate); player 2D gun exempt. Existing 8/sec impact limiter confirmed firing + sufficient for impacts.
4. INAUDIBLE DROP. Pre-existing play_world audibility cull (gain < 0.01 -> no voice) retained; its computed attenuation now also feeds the steal-priority gain.

REVISED THREADING CONTRACT (audio.h): added the 'reload' SPSC flag spec. Per-slot sample_idx/loop/cursor have a single live writer (audio thread) once published; main hands off live-slot changes via pending_*+reload, writes free slots directly (alive last). Documented the benign residual (steal landing in the exact buffer a one-shot finishes can drop at most one SFX; self-recovers next alloc, no corruption/stuck slot).

VALIDATION (./build/new_privateer --system troy, /tmp/np_troy_perf.log, ~57s, real NPC furball, 8 ship kills):
- Clean build (cmake --build build -j), only pre-existing -Wmissing-braces warnings.
- 'steal spin timed out' occurrences: 0 (path gone).
- FPS during heavy combat: 58-60 (34x60, 21x59, 2x58). One isolated ~7fps window at peak projectile density — NOT audio (filed np-p8z: physics/per-event-log spike).
- Engine hum loop (voice 512 / slot 0) started once, never re-allocated/culled — survives saturation.
- Original SFX all play (11/11 originals loaded; gun/impact/explosion events fired throughout).
- Instrumentation proved budget/cull: '[audio] furball: voices peak 22/24, world starts dropped 0 (budget 8/frame)'; sfx coalescing suppressed up to 200+ NPC shots/window. Throttled to significant-change ~1/sec.

FILES CHANGED: src/audio.h (threading contract + voice-steal doc), src/audio.cpp (reload field, mixer swap/guarded retire, non-blocking weakest-victim alloc, split publish free/steal paths, per-frame budget + furball instrumentation in set_listener, incoming-gain at call sites), src/sfx.cpp (NPC-gunfire coalescing gate).

BEFORE: full pool -> every steal spins ~5ms on game thread -> furball = hundreds of ms stall/frame -> user-visible lag + 'steal spin timed out' spam.
AFTER: non-blocking alloc, 58-60fps through the furball, hum protected, full original SFX, zero main-thread audio stalls.

Constraints honored: pool stays 24 (fixed the blocking, didn't starve mixer), audio-thread mixer still lock-free/alloc-free, engine hum never culled, sfx facade + gameplay call sites unchanged, minimal targeted diffs, house comment style, no new deps.

title: Save/load: JSON save slots, autosave on dock
description: Serialize Player state + current system + docked status via existing src/json.{h,cpp} to ~/Library/Application Support/new_privateer/saves/. Acceptance: save→quit→load round-trips credits/cargo/rep/location bit-exact.
notes:
Implemented save/load (np-ymp.1). ACCEPTANCE MET: save->load round-trips credits/cargo/rep/location bit-exact (proven by tools/test_savegame.cpp — field-by-field log, ALL CHECKS PASSED).

FILES:
- NEW src/savegame.{h,cpp}: savegame::save/load/peek + slot_path/saves_dir. Saves to ~/Library/Application Support/new_privateer/saves/save_<n>.json (slot 0=autosave, 1+=manual). Atomic write (temp+rename). Format version int + unix timestamp + human label. Rep serialized as object keyed by faction NAME (faction::to_name) for enum-reorder stability. credits stored as a JSON STRING (parser stores numbers as double; string+strtoll guarantees int64 bit-exactness). Tiny local JsonWriter (json.cpp is parse-only by design — see its header — so the writer lives in savegame.cpp rather than widening json's documented scope; DISCOVERED-FROM note below).
- src/docking.cpp: autosave hook on the Docking->Docked transition (slot 0). Logs '[save] autosaved at <base> (<credits> cr)'.
- src/main.cpp: CLI --load <slot> / --continue (slot 0). Boot peeks the slot's recorded system and loads that world UNLESS --system is explicit (PRECEDENCE: explicit --system > saved system > default troy, documented in init_cb). Player state applied over new_game(); when --system explicitly wins, player.current_system is reconciled to the loaded world. Graceful: bad/missing save -> keep new game, never crash.
- src/base_screens.cpp: minimal concourse UI — 'Save game (slot 1)' button + last-autosave readout (label + timestamp via peek()).
- CMakeLists.txt: added src/savegame.cpp.

VALIDATION:
- Headless harness tools/test_savegame.cpp: mutate every field -> save -> fresh default -> load -> bit-exact compare = ALL CHECKS PASSED. Failure paths: missing-file load=false (state intact), corrupt/truncated load=false (no crash), version>supported refused.
- Real boot: hand-crafted slot-0 autosave, launched binary with --continue -> '[save] resumed slot 0 — 999999 cr, ship centurion, system troy, base achilles', no crash. Verified --system override precedence (explicit world wins).
- Clean build (cmake --build build -j).

DISCOVERED-FROM: src/json.{h,cpp} is parse-only (header explicitly excludes JSON emit). Added a small local JsonWriter in savegame.cpp with proper escaping rather than third-party deps or widening json's scope. If a 2nd writer consumer appears, promote to json::Writer then.

title: Encounter director: per-system spawn tables, distance spawn/despawn, autopilot interrupts
description: Procedural NPC traffic instead of JSON-placed ships. Files: src/encounters.{h,cpp}; spawn-table block in system JSON. Belt=pirates, station lanes=merchants/militia.
notes:
Encounter director shipped (planning-agent-6dc9be).

FILES
- NEW src/encounters.{h,cpp}: the director. init(system) parses spawn tables; tick(registry,player_pos,dt,spawn,despawn) maintains a live population. Host/director split: director owns WHEN/WHERE/WHO (timing, region placement, weighted faction+class draws, budget); host (main.cpp encounter_spawn/encounter_despawn) owns WHAT = the literal np-eag.1 recipe (claim sprite slot, attach atlas, ship::spawn, faction+AI, registry.spawn/despawn). Director TU has zero AppState dependency.
- src/system_def.{h,cpp}: new EncounterRuleDef/EncounterWeight + StarSystem.encounters; JSON parser for the 'encounters' block.
- src/threat.{h,cpp}: implemented hostiles_near() for real (was np-opa.3 stub) + added set_world(registry,rep). Iterates registry, faction::stance_npc_vs_player==Hostile && within radius. Call sites UNCHANGED (autopilot gate just works).
- src/main.cpp: include + host hooks + encounters::init/threat::set_world at system load (with atlas preload for encounter-only classes) + encounters::tick in Flight loop after ship_ai (standalone call, not nested in registry iteration). Mode-gated to Flight by the existing return.
- assets/systems/troy.json: 4 rules — belt pirates (talon/orion), lane merchants (tarsus/galaxy on Achilles->Hector->Helen), lane militia (talon, Achilles<->Hector), roaming raiders (pirate/hunter, anywhere).
- CMakeLists.txt: + src/encounters.cpp.

DESIGN
- Placement: spawn on an 8-15km shell around the player (sub-pixel at that range => no visible pop-in), region-biased (belt=clamp into AABB, lane=lerp 65% onto nearest segment, anywhere=as-is). Region also GATES activation (belt pirates only arm when player within 25km of the belt). Patrol-seeded ships flip to Engage via existing perception+stance and fly in under their own power.
- Despawn: distance(>40km) AND not Engage/BreakOff => retire + free slot. Engaged ships are immune (never yanked from a visible fight). Generation-safe slot-map despawn; standalone call avoids mid-iteration mutation.
- Budget: per-rule max_concurrent + global k_director_max=8 + registry hard cap 64. No per-frame heap churn (rule state+id lists reused; RNG is a member, distributions stack-local).

VALIDATION (Troy, driven via dev_remote /camera/set)
- Spawns: '[encounter] spawned pirate talon @ 9km, pop 1/8', orion @14km, etc. Belt+lane rules armed on arrival.
- Population held within budget: director_pop peaked at exactly 8/8, never exceeded.
- Despawns on drift: '[encounter] despawned lane merchants @ 113km (drifted), pop 7/8' freeing slots for new spawns.
- Threat gate LIVE: threat::hostiles_near(8km)=TRUE with the placed pirate fleet ~7km from spawn (=> autopilot refuses/drops); tracks to false when no hostile within the bubble.
- Stability: ~2.5min soak with 18 teleports across regions => 35 spawns / 20 despawns, ships peaked 33 (<64 cap), steady 60fps, zero crashes/asserts/stale-handle BUGs.
- Screenshot: radar shows multiple contacts at range while screen stays clear (placement strategy confirmed).

NOTES
- No ASAN: CMake has no sanitizer option; soak run was non-instrumented (noted, not cheap to wire here).
- Patrol==Idle is still a placeholder in ship_ai (pre-existing); neutral director ships loiter until threatened. Fine for v1; OrbitAnchor patrol is future work.

description: Bind to docs/privateer_db/cargo.toml commodities (runtime loader or build-time convert). Hand-authored price biases per base (mining base: cheap ore, dear food); swap in extracted BASES.IFF pricing when E2 lands.
notes:
Commodity exchange implemented (assignee planning-agent-6dc9be).

DESIGN (data-driven, no per-base price tables in C++):
- assets/data/commodity_prices.json (NEW, hand-authored + tunable): canonical per-CATEGORY base price, global buy/sell spread (18%), and base ARCHETYPES (each a map category->{price_mult,stock}). Documented because cargo.toml _trailing_hex is undecoded (privateer_db README). Archetypes: 'mining' (cheap RAWMAT/CAPGOOD, dear FOOD/LUXURY) + 'agricultural' (cheap FOOD, dear RAWMAT/MICRO).

- src/economy.{h,cpp} (NEW): economy::price(base,commodity)->{buy,sell,avail}. buy=round(catbase*mult); sell=round(buy*(1-spread)) so same-base flip loses money; avail=archetype stock, decremented per-session via record_purchase (0=not buyable, always sellable). Two-col trade table: name/category/buy/sell/avail/held + Buy1/Buy10/Sell1/SellAll. Buttons disabled when unaffordable / over cap / out of stock / nothing held; click path also logs refusals. Sell price greens when above bought_at avg. Running totals (credits, cargo X/Y) up top; ui_click sfx on every txn. ALL mutation via player:: helpers only (can_afford/spend_credits/add_credits/add_cargo/remove_cargo) so np-ymp.1 save/load stays correct.
- CMakeLists: added src/economy.cpp.
- main.cpp: economy::load + register_exchange_screen after commodity::load; include economy.h.

ARBITRAGE NET +1900 credits => PASS.

title: Sprite-with-lights rendering pipeline (Privateer/Homeworld aesthetic)
description:
Pivot: most objects (stations, ships) become camera-facing sprite billboards with additively-blended animated light overlays. Keeps the current 3D pipeline intact (planets + asteroids stay 3D) but shifts the STATION/SHIP visual identity to a layered 2D approach that:

  - plays to our strengths (we have a pixel-artist agent + bloom post pass)
  - looks genuinely cinematic at low content cost (FTL / Stellaris / OG Privateer vibes)
  - dramatically simplifies the content pipeline — no more OBJ/mtl/materials.json/sidecars per ship

Architecture sketch:
  struct SpriteObject {
    sg_view hull_tex;           // RGBA8, alpha-blend
    sg_view lights_tex;         // RGBA8, additive — painted lights
    std::vector<LightSpot> anim;// code-animated blink/pulse lights
    HMM_Vec3 position; float scale; float alpha;
  };
  struct LightSpot { float u, v; uint32 rgba; float size, blink_hz, phase; };

Render order: opaque 3D (asteroids, planets) → sprite hulls (alpha-blended, sorted back-to-front) → sprite lights (additive, no depth write) → existing post/bloom pass.

Billboarding: always face the camera, no bank/pitch. Keeps the look clean 2D, matches OG Privateer. Sprite quads' world size is  units across regardless of aspect (aspect comes from the texture).

Scope for this epic:
  - Stations (mining_base, pirate_base) → sprites
  - Ships (when we add them) → sprites
  - Keep 3D: planets (sphere.obj does the job), asteroids (parallax feels good), sun, skybox, atmospheres.

title: Decode MNVR maneuver-class semantics via resident DGROUP vtables (PRCD.EXE)

Vtables live in the RESIDENT DGROUP (not the overlay carve). Load PRCD.EXE resident in Ghidra, read the vtable function pointers at the DGROUP offsets, decompile each class's +0x0c/+0x14 to recover real maneuver semantics (turn-to-target/throttle/evade/afterburner/fire). title: Locate MNVR byte-stream deserializer / class registry (PRCD.EXE)

title: Jump-through mechanic: approach gate → transition to linked system
description:
Gameplay flow:
  1. Player autopilots to (or flies to) a jump-point nav
  2. When within trigger distance (~500 u) and travelling below cruise speed, a 'Jump Ready' prompt appears
  3. Press J (or auto-engage on arrival?) to initiate jump
  4. Brief effect: camera flash + audio sting (deferred — just a quick fade for v0)
  5. Destination system is loaded (lazy, via the Galaxy loader)
  6. Player is placed at the reciprocal jump gate in the destination system, facing into the system
  7. Camera position / velocity reset sensibly

Reciprocal matching:
  - If target nav has a 'links_to: {system, nav}' pair, arrival is at that exact nav
  - Otherwise, arrive at the first jump_point nav in the destination system that links back to our origin
  - If no reciprocal exists, log a warning and arrive at (0,0,0) near the sun

Hostile-gate reuse: like autopilot (np-opa.3), jumping should be blocked if hostiles are too close — Privateer tradition.
acceptance_criteria: Flying within ~500 u of a gate and stopping triggers a Jump prompt. Press J → fade out → destination system loaded → player placed at reciprocal gate. Round-trip (Troy → Pyrenees → Troy) works and lands you back near the original gate. Jump refused if hostile stub ever returns true.
notes:
DONE (planning-agent-6dc9be). Jump-through mechanic shipped.

FILES
  + src/jump.{h,cpp}      — pure eligibility oracle (jump twin of docking::can_request): evaluate() returns a Status verdict {Ready/NotJumpNav/NoRoute/TooFar/Hostiles} + dest id/name + reciprocal arrival nav; prompt() turns it into the NAV-MFD line. No GPU/scene knowledge — trivially testable.
  ~ src/main.cpp          — pending_jump_{system,nav} state; execute_jump() (reuses load_and_build_system from np-6al.1 -> player persists; places camera AT reciprocal gate, +1500u toward system center, facing into-system, 60u/s inward drift); Loading-mode hyperspace flash in frame_stub (clear colour blown white at entry, ease-out fade — 'JUMPING TO <dest>...'); J keypress handler (re-checks eligibility, queues jump, requests Loading, sfx); HUD NAV-MFD reuses dock_prompt slot for the jump prompt on jump navs; --dev-jump-soak/--dev-jump-interval headless J driver + update_dev_jump_soak().
  ~ src/sfx.{h,cpp}       — sfx::jump() hyperspace sting (reuses cruise_windup.wav @0.9 gain; no new asset — swap file later if a bespoke whoosh lands).
  ~ CMakeLists.txt        — + src/jump.cpp.
  + tools/test_jump.cpp   — standalone harness (clang++, like test_autopilot): all 6 cases PASS.

DESIGN
  - Eligibility gate mirrors autopilot's: jump kind + surveyed galaxy edge + within trigger range + threat::hostiles_near gate (SAME oracle as autopilot/np-ma2.3 -> can't jump mid-furball; refusal logged '[jump] refused: hostiles near').
  - Execution rides the np-6al.1 deferred frame-boundary path (load_and_build_system) + np-eag.2 Loading mode. Player ship/cargo/credits/rep persist (clear_except_player keeps slot 0). Cinematic = white-flash fade in the existing Loading stub (simple, satisfying, zero new render passes).
  - TRIGGER RANGE: bead floated ~500u but autopilot eases to a stop within k_arrival_radius_m=5000u; 500u would make criterion 5 (autopilot->J prompt) impossible. Set k_trigger_range_m=6000u (just past autopilot arrival) so the A->J flow composes. Documented in jump.h.

VALIDATION
  - Unit (tools/test_jump): Ready ('PRESS J TO JUMP - Pyrenees'), TooFar (50000u>6000u), NoRoute (Troy 'War Jump' dangling), NotJumpNav (station -> no prompt), Hostiles ('JUMP: HOSTILES NEAR', threat stub), reciprocal round-trip troy/'Pyrenees Jump'->pyrenees/'Troy Jump'->troy/'Pyrenees Jump'. ALL PASS.
  - Live (--dev-jump-soak 5): 5 reciprocal jumps Troy<->Pyrenees. Logs show '[jump] troy -> pyrenees via Pyrenees Jump', flight->loading->flight, '=== switching ===' teardown (frees fields/sprites/atlases/NPCs), rebuild, '[jump] arrived in Pyrenees at gate Troy Jump — pos -59117,19706,78823 facing into-system'. Reciprocal arrival positions deterministic & identical across repeats (Troy gate pos (99164,66110,132219); Pyrenees gate (-59117,19706,78823)). Player persists every hop (2000cr, tarsus). Clean quit; error/leak/assert/NaN scan clean — no new leak on the jump path beyond np-6al.1's audited teardown.
  - HUD J-prompt screenshot not captured: dev_remote has no key injection (need N to select nav), so per the bead's 'else rely on logs' allowance the exact prompt strings are proven by the unit test + eligibility logs.
  - Hostile-gate live: reuses the np-ma2.3-validated threat::hostiles_near; refusal path proven by unit case 5 + shared seam.

NOTES
  - Autopilot integration (criterion 5): J handler gates on autopilot Idle, so you fly in with A, drop to Idle within 5000u, then the 6000u jump prompt is waiting — press J.
  - discovered-from: np-6al.3.1 (stale test_autopilot.cpp build command — threat.cpp went live in np-ma2.3, standalone link now needs faction+ship_registry; game binary unaffected).
  - Satisfies the last hard dependency of np-zte.3 (full-loop playtest).

title: Autopilot-to-nav on 'A' key (hostile-gated, strafe moves to Q/E)
description:
With N now cycling the selected nav (see np-opa.2), pressing 'A' engages autopilot TOWARD the currently-selected nav. Classic Privateer muscle memory.

Behaviour when A is pressed:
  - If no nav selected → no-op, flash a 'no nav selected' warning in the HUD
  - If hostiles within threat range → refuse to engage, flash 'hostiles detected — cannot autopilot' (OG Privateer behaviour)
  - Otherwise → rotate camera smoothly toward the selected nav, engage cruise, keep accelerating until within arrival distance (~5000 u), then auto-drop to normal speed

Key remap (A was previously strafe-left):
  - Q = strafe left (new)
  - E = strafe right (new, currently D)
  - A = autopilot (new)
  - D is freed up; reserve for later (maybe 'dock' when at a base)

Hostile gate stub:
  - New tiny file threat.{h,cpp} with 'bool hostiles_near(HMM_Vec3 pos, float radius)' — for now ALWAYS returns false (we have no NPCs). When we add enemies later this function grows; autopilot's caller never changes.

Any manual flight input (W/S/Q/E/space/shift/mouse) immediately cancels autopilot.
acceptance_criteria: A key engages autopilot toward selected nav; no-ops gracefully when none selected or hostiles present (stub always false for now). Q/E strafe left/right (was A/D). Autopilot rotates smoothly, cruises, auto-drops within 5000 u. Any WASD-era manual input cancels autopilot. On-screen controls hint updated.
notes:
Implemented by planning-agent-6dc9be (code-puppy-3e591e).

- NEW src/autopilot.{h,cpp}: nav cruise autopilot state machine (Idle/Cruising/Arriving). Separate from docking (traversal controller ending in free flight vs docking's terminal approach ending in a mode flip) but mirrors its discipline: free-fn namespace over a plain struct AppState owns, controls_locked() mutes pilot input, shortest-arc facing slerp.
- NEW tools/test_autopilot.cpp: offline harness (mirrors test_docking.cpp), deterministic proof of engage->cruise->arrive + refusals + cancel.

title: Track 2: decode MNVR maneuver bytecode via PRCD.EXE disasm (Ghidra)
description: Head-start from np-zvv: 35 unique MNVR scripts (lengths 120/176/191/199B), entry opcodes cluster 0x0d/0x0e/0x0f (+rare 0x0b,0x09). MANEUVER.IFF gives 3 morale-tier scripts to diff. Verbatim hex in gitignored ai_dump/privateer_ai.json. Find bytecode interpreter in PRCD.EXE, recover opcode->operand-width, decode scripts 1:1. Then wire MNVR timings into k_break_duration/k_firing_max.
notes: CNST distance-scale CONFIRMED (code-puppy-1e3d06, disasm of resident PRCD.EXE). REFUTES x10. Storage: ship+0x2->pilotdef; pilotdef+0x17->CNST 16B block (loader 0xb37f1); f0@block+0, f1@block+2, stored RAW. Consumption (resident, not overlay): f1 detection func @0x1ce8c does dist via lcall 0x4c5b:0x296, sar eax,8 (/256) then cmp f1 (jg in-range) -> detection = f1 world units (1500). f0 engage func @0x1d1f8 does f0<<8 (x256) + selfR<<8 + targetR<<8, cmp dist jge out -> engage=(f0+R1+R2) world units. Scale = 2^8=256 fixed-point (power of two), LINEAR distance (not squared, no x100), NO imul-by-10/shift-add-10/load-time scaling anywhere. detection(1500)>engage(600) holds. Defaults [0xe50]=f0(600),[0xe52]=f1(1500)=MANEUVER.IFF fallback. Wiring: f1->perception, f0->engage in Privateer world units; the user's ~15000 cull = ~10:1 unit ratio (new_privateer vs Privateer), a unit conversion NOT engine x10 -> use f1->15000,f0->6000 in our units. docs/ai_model.md updated (new 7.9, f0/f1 promoted to [C], 7.3 corrected: +0x17=CNST ptr). re/ verified gitignored. np-d2w stays in_progress (MNVR opcode decode 7.7 still open).

comments.author: Mike Pfaffenberger
comments.text: HUD distance x10 session (planning-agent-6dc9be / code-puppy-a591e3): REFUTED. No x10 on any distance in PRCD.EXE. Display path uses magnitude>>8 (file 0x3329f/0x20cd8/0x2f8b0/0x43737: lcall 0x4c5b:0x296 -> sar eax,8 -> push raw value -> VDU). Same >>8 world-unit scale the AI compares to CNST f1=1500/f0=600 (s7.9). Magnitude helper verified @file 0x57646 (alpha-max-beta-min). Every imul/mul-by-10 in the binary is text-row layout (0x71d5d/0x72496/0x733ae line-height 10), array stride 10 (0xd8a51..,0x1e06e), percentage math (0x1ca5c) or itoa (0xb40a4..) -- never a distance. dpjudas CockpitScreen.cpp corroborates: 'Range: <dist>m' = raw length, cull 10000. So detection internal 1500 -> shows ~1500 (NOT 15000); engage 600 -> ~600. The 10:1 is a unit convention, not an engine multiply. Documented docs/ai_model.md s7.10. re/ gitignored (verified).

Pre-existing tooling gap, not gameplay.

title: dev_remote port doc drift: header says default 8765 but it binds 47001
notes: Discovered-from np-9cu.2 (commodity exchange validation). dev_remote.h documents start(int port=8765) but the running game bound 127.0.0.1:47001 — screenshot scripts must parse the actual port from the '[dev_remote] listening on' log line. Low priority doc/code mismatch.

title: Real concourse art for bases
description: Replace the procedural placeholder concourses (tools/gen_placeholder_concourse.py output at assets/bases/<id>/concourse.png) with real Privateer-style pixel-art concourse backgrounds for achilles/hector/helen (and future bases). Placeholder art was committed in np-9cu.4 so the base-screen framework had something to blit; hotspot layout + base.json schema are stable. Pixel-art pass should run through tools/pixelart pipeline. Keep the same normalized hotspot rects (art just needs to visually suggest the doorways at those regions).

title: Extraction parsers: ships.py, guns.py, sectors.py, bases.py
description: Extend tools/import_privateer_db per privateer_db README roadmap. Hybrid policy: extracted data validates/refines hand-authored content, never blocks it. Refs: dpjudas/WCPrivateer, HCL format docs.

title: Galaxy map UI: graph overlay of systems + jump routes
description:
Companion to np-opa.2's in-system navmap. A whole new overlay at a different key (probably 'G' for galaxy?) showing:
  - Every known system as a labelled node, positioned by galaxy_position
  - Every jump-gate edge as a line between its endpoints
  - Current system highlighted
  - Optional: route plotter — click a target system, shortest-path Dijkstra highlights the chain of jumps needed
  - Sector boundaries / colouring for visual grouping (Troy sector vs Clarke sector etc.)

Can share rendering primitives with the in-system navmap (navmap.{h,cpp}) — just a different dataset. Keep the overlay code in one file if it stays under 600 LOC, split if it grows.
acceptance_criteria: Press G → galaxy map overlay appears. All seeded systems drawn as labelled nodes with jump edges between them. Current system visually distinct. Pressing G again closes. Does not interfere with navmap (M) or debug panel (Ctrl+M).

title: Seed canonical Privateer system roster (extract from WCU or hand-author)
description:
Original Privateer has roughly 60 systems across 6 sectors (Troy, Pyrenees, Capella, Castor, Pollux, Eden — plus Gemini fringe). Each has a known set of navs and jump connections.

Sources to mine:
  - ../privateer_wcu assets — Vega Strike port probably has system JSONs
  - The original game's CIC/system data (fan wikis)
  - RimRunner's Privateer Remake (if accessible)

Strategy:
  - Write a tools/import_wcu_systems.py that walks the WCU system files, extracts nav positions + jump links, and emits our format
  - Fall back to hand-authoring the first 5-10 systems for Troy's immediate neighbourhood if auto-extract is infeasible
  - Minimum viable for this epic: Troy + Pyrenees + New Detroit + 2 others, connected in a simple line or small cluster

This is mostly a data-entry task once the schema from np-opa.1 + Galaxy model from this epic's child #1 are solid.
acceptance_criteria: At least 5 systems exist as valid system JSONs (Troy + 4 others). galaxy.json lists them with jump-gate edges. Jumping through Troy's gates lands in real, distinct systems. At least one multi-hop path exists (A → B → C).

title: hide_ui flag on /screenshot endpoint
description: Now that the debug panel is hidden by default, only the sdtx HUD + controls hint remain overlaid. For clean screenshots it'd be nice to toggle those off in the screenshot request rather than needing a permanent keybind.
acceptance_criteria: POST /screenshot accepts {hide_ui: true}. When set, sdtx layer is not drawn for that frame only. No permanent state change.

title: /camera/look_at dev_remote endpoint
description: Currently /camera/set takes yaw+pitch, so to aim at a specific world-space target I have to do atan2 math by hand in shell. A look_at endpoint accepting (target_xyz, up?) would be much more ergonomic for screenshotting.
acceptance_criteria: POST /camera/look_at with JSON {target:[x,y,z], up?:[x,y,z]} computes yaw/pitch from the current camera position and the target point. Optional 'pos' field to also move the camera in the same call.

title: Binary texture cache (.npttex) for faster warm start
description: After Phase D mesh cache, PNG decode dominates mining_base warm-load (65ms). Could cache decompressed RGBA pixel data next to each PNG and skip stb_image. Trade-off: more disk. Probably YAGNI unless cold/warm start matters more.
acceptance_criteria: Optional .npttex sidecar next to each PNG, mtime-invalidated. Warm load of mining_base drops below 15ms. Guarded by a build flag or cmdline switch since the disk cost is nontrivial.

title: Procedural normal map generation for planet surfaces
description: The agricultural planet preset generates a procedural diffuse texture but ships it with no normal map — the sphere mesh gets the flat-normal 1x1 fallback. The Phase C TBN shader is wired up and ready; we just need to generate a matching bumpy normal map from the same noise field.
acceptance_criteria: planet_texture::generate also produces a normal map. Planet surface shows visible micro-relief at grazing sun angles. Works for every preset (agricultural/barren/etc) without per-preset special cases.

title: Import WCU shared textures path for un-localized materials
description: pirate_base has 2 submeshes (tex0_0/tex1_0) that reference textures living in the shared VS textures dir, not in units/hospital_base/. Import script currently only searches the unit-local dir, so these come through with empty diffuse slots.
acceptance_criteria: tools/import_wcu_meshes.sh also searches VS shared textures path when a material name isn't found locally. Re-importing pirate_base fills in D7/S0/G0/N0 → D7/SX/GX/NX appropriately.

title: Missiles render as glow billboards, not a mesh/trail
description: np-zte.2 renders in-flight missiles via the additive tracer glow path (per-type tint: DF white / HS orange / IR cyan, size 22). Good enough for v1 but a small missile mesh + smoke/exhaust trail would read far better as 'a missile streaking at you'. Cosmetic; no gameplay impact.

title: Source/produce final SFX set
description: Replace the procedural CC0 stand-in WAVs (tools/gen_test_sfx.py) with produced/sourced final SFX: laser_fire, impact_shield, impact_armor, explosion_small, explosion_big, cruise_windup, ui_click, engine_hum (loop-clean). The sfx.cpp facade maps events->samples in one place, so only load_all()'s file list (and the asset files) change when finals land — no gameplay re-wiring needed. Keep PCM16 mono/stereo @ device-friendly rate; engine_hum must loop click-free.

title: Hand-written atmospheric-param live tuner in debug panel
description: atm_thickness / atm_color / atm_strength currently only tweakable by editing troy.json and restarting. Would be nice as sliders in the debug panel's per-planet section, mirroring what we already do for ships.
acceptance_criteria: meshes/planets/sphere.obj entry in the Ship Sizer panel exposes the three atm_* params when the placed mesh has a planet_preset. Copy-JSON button emits the atm_* block.
